about: The fitting room: complex creatures stand in front of the camera, as their models come and with tools in the hand, and play one animation each, booth after booth (fit_spec.py says which). It is how an attack is made to match its animation before it goes into a game: what the model holds, what a mounted weapon looks like in the hand, at which millisecond the stroke lands, how far it carries the creature. The whole play is photographed eight times a second (bursts): playtest_frames {runId, fromSeconds, toSeconds, crop} puts a booth's frames side by side, each labelled with its play second to a hundredth. Prints: FT <booth> when a booth opens (the log's clock runs five to six seconds ahead of the play seconds of the frames), FT_S every time a skill's graph runs: at the moment given as graphAtMs, and once for every moment when a list was given (a triple stroke with three moments prints three times each time it plays). To look at other creatures or animations, change SHOWS and MOMENTS in fit_spec.py and run make_fit.py; creature_animations lists the animations of a creature and what was already seen of them.
